strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear visualization of complementary strengths between VFMs and VLMs through t-SNE analysis
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 diverse benchmarks with consistent ~10% average improvement over CLIP baseline
Principled probabilistic approach using optimal transport that is model-agnostic, scalable, and avoids expensive feature concatenation
Thorough ablation studies (Table 2) effectively validating each component's contribution and demonstrating necessity of joint learning
Training-free method with practical applicability in resource-constrained scenarios requiring no fine-tuning or additional annotations

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies established optimal transport techniques (Caron et al. 2020) and standard GMM modeling to a new problem setting without significant methodological innovation

Insufficient justification for key design choices: (1) why maximize Tr(Q^T P) + λTr(Q^T Y) rather than minimize a divergence, (2) why shared diagonal covariance is appropriate, (3) why GMM is the right choice for visual distributions

Inadequate evaluation of multiple VFMs: only DINOv2 used in main experiments despite claiming flexibility; Eq. 6 extension presented but not empirically validated; no guidance on setting {ηi}, {λi} weights

Missing critical baselines: no comparison with simple weighted averaging of CLIP and DINOv2 predictions, and no direct quantitative comparison with DINO-assisted prompt learning mentioned as motivation
Limited experimental scope: transductive-only setting prevents assessment of broader applicability; inductive ZSL results absent despite being practically important
No statistical significance testing: single runs reported without error bars or confidence intervals, problematic for potentially small test sets (e.g., Aircraft dataset)
Initialization bias toward semantics: P(0) initialized with semantic distribution Y, undermining claims of symmetric mutual reinforcement between visual and semantic branches
Hyperparameter sensitivity despite 'training-free' claims: performance degrades significantly when λ > 0.7; no principled dataset-agnostic selection strategy provided for new datasets
Missing computational analysis: no runtime comparisons with baselines; no analysis of computational overhead from iterative optimization procedure despite scalability claims

Incomplete investigation of method limitations: modest gains on fine-grained datasets (Aircraft +4.26%) unexplored; no analysis of dataset characteristics determining success; no failure case discussion

strengths: Clear motivation using t-SNE visualization showing complementary strengths of CLIP and DINOv2
Practical framework that is training-free (in the sense of not requiring fine-tuning) and model-agnostic, operating on probability distributions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 diverse datasets with extensive baseline comparisons
Solid average performance: ~10% accuracy improvement over CLIP baseline
Detailed ablation studies (Table 2) demonstrating importance of visual features, fusion strategy, and joint learning
Clear presentation of algorithm and optimization procedure with explicit implementation details
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (GMM, Optimal Transport) without introducing new perspectives to zero-shot learning
Core design choices lack justification: Why GMM specifically? Why shared diagonal covariance? Why not simpler weighted averaging (concatenation baseline achieves 75.54% vs OTFusion's 74.95%)?

Misleading 'training-free' claim: method performs alternating optimization (GMM E-step, Sinkhorn solve, M-step) on test data for multiple iterations; computational cost of test-time adaptation not discussed

Hyperparameter robustness claims contradicted: Figure 2 shows significant sensitivity to λ on EuroSAT (drop >13%) and Flowers102 (drop ~8%), contradicting 'remarkably stable' claim; choice λ=0.8 falls in unstable region for some datasets

Inconsistent and marginal improvements: Aircraft shows only +1.41% with ResNet50; EuroSAT outliers (+31-38%) suggest dataset bias; ResNet50 benefits disproportionately (+15.6%) compared to ViT (+10%), indicating architecture-dependent results; no significance testing or confidence intervals provided

Weak theoretical foundation: 'mutual reinforcement' explanation is intuitive but unrigorous; no convergence analysis, optimality guarantees, or formal justification for why joint optimization improves zero-shot accuracy

Unfair comparisons: DINO-assisted prompt learning dismissed for computational cost without quantifying OTFusion's own test-time overhead; claim about generalization across foundation models unverified
Critical ablation missing: simple weighted averaging baseline (α·P + β·Y) not tested, making OT justification questionable given concatenation performs nearly as well
Scalability claims unsupported: no runtime comparisons, no analysis of memory scaling with test set size or number of classes; claimed 'lightweight' and 'low-resource' benefits undemonstrated
GMM modeling details unclear: fitting procedure, convergence criteria, initialization strategy not specified; affects reproducibility and suggests potential hidden hyperparameter tuning
Limited failure analysis: no discussion of when/why OTFusion fails, which dataset properties enable success, or generalization beyond standard benchmarks
Visual evidence weak: t-SNE sensitive to initialization and perplexity; quantitative cluster quality metrics (silhouette score, Davies-Bouldin) would strengthen cluster separation claims
Incomplete technical exposition: final classification implicit (argmax over Q?), numerical stability of Sinkhorn not discussed, projection to doubly stochastic constraint unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies genuine complementarity between VFMs (tight visual clusters) and VLMs (semantic alignment), effectively illustrated via t-SNE visualization
Elegant probabilistic framework: Operating in probability space via optimal transport is intuitive and enables flexible multi-model integration without architectural constraints
Comprehensive experimental validation: 11 diverse datasets, 15+ baselines, two backbones, consistent ~10% average improvement with rigorous ablation studies
Practical training-free approach: No fine-tuning or additional annotations required, valuable for resource-constrained deployment
Thorough analysis: Parameter sensitivity analysis demonstrates robustness; convergence analysis shows rapid (5 iterations) and stable optimization; ablations clearly justify joint learning necessity
Clear presentation: Well-written with effective motivation, clear methodology, and comprehensive experimental setup
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (GMM, optimal transport, Sinkhorn, entropy regularization) are well-established; primary contribution is their combination rather than methodological innovation
Missing critical comparison: DINO-assisted prompt learning (Imam et al., 2024)—a directly relevant baseline addressing the same problem—is absent from main results despite being cited as related work

Scalability limitations acknowledged but inadequately addressed: Equal-weight fusion (ηᵢ=1), no dynamic gating, and naive concatenation become prohibitively expensive with multiple VFMs; fundamentally limits extensibility

Insufficient analysis of failure modes: Minimal improvements on Aircraft (+1.41% ResNet50), inconsistent results on DTD; no investigation of when/why the method underperforms or when concatenation outperforms OTFusion
Lack of statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variance analysis; unclear if results are single-run or multi-seed averages; critical for rigorous benchmarking

Unjustified structural assumptions: Shared diagonal covariance matrix and C=number-of-classes are strong simplifications with no sensitivity analysis; no comparison to alternative clustering approaches (k-means, spectral methods)
Incomplete hyperparameter justification: ε=0.01 and λ=0.8 chosen empirically without principled selection strategy; Figure 2 shows λ performance drops at 0.8, creating inconsistency
Missing computational analysis: No runtime measurements, memory requirements, or complexity analysis despite claiming 'lightweight' efficiency
Underdocumented initialization sensitivity: Semantic initialization (P⁽⁰⁾←Y) dependency unclear; no ablation on initialization strategy robustness
Unexplained dataset-dependent variance: Large backbone-dependent differences (e.g., ImageNet: +10% ViT vs. +16% ResNet50) without analysis; generalization claims need stronger justification

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear illustrations of complementary strengths between VLMs (semantic alignment) and VFMs (fine-grained visual features)
Comprehensive experimental validation across 26 benchmarks spanning natural images, medical pathology, and remote sensing domains with consistent improvements
Training-free and prior-free framework applicable to black-box models, eliminating need for fine-tuning or manual weight selection
Thorough ablation studies (Fig. 4, Table 5) systematically demonstrating the importance of each component (VFM introduction, self-adaptive weighting, joint learning)
Practical efficiency: rapid convergence (5-10 iterations), competitive computational overhead, sample-wise inference
Clear presentation with detailed methodology and reproducibility-supporting implementation details in appendix
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: optimal transport application rather than methodological innovation; squared Frobenius form (Eq. 7) is minor modification; MM algorithm is standard practice

Unfair experimental comparisons: SOTA uses multiple models (e.g., CLIP-1+DINOv3) vs. single-model baselines; improvement conflates model quality with fusion benefits; missing simple ensemble baselines (averaging, weighted averaging)

Self-adaptive weighting mechanism lacks theoretical justification: no principled explanation for why lower transport cost implies higher model reliability; post-hoc justification in 6.2 rather than upfront motivation

GMM fitting for high-dimensional VFM features inadequately addressed: no analysis of sample complexity for covariance estimation, K selection unspecified, diagonal covariance assumption introduced late; marginal improvement (+0.3-0.8%) from joint learning (Eq. 8) questions its necessity

Limited generalizability: transductive setting requires unlabeled test data (impractical constraint); inductive setting (Table 4) shows only comparable performance to DMN/COSMIC, not consistent superiority

Experimental rigor concerns: no error bars or significance tests; single-run results; unexplained performance degradation on Aircraft (-2.1%); hyperparameter sensitivity (τ, ϵ, K, initialization) not analyzed

Lack of theoretical grounding: connection between minimizing transport cost and classification accuracy assumed not derived; convergence to stationary points may trap in local minima; no analysis of method success/failure conditions

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 26 benchmarks spanning three distinct domains (natural images, medical pathology, remote sensing) demonstrates broad applicability and generalization potential
Strong and consistent empirical improvements over competitive baselines, with average gains of 7.5% on natural images and 17% on remote sensing compared to best single models
Well-motivated problem: clearly illustrates complementary strengths of VLMs (semantic alignment) vs VFMs (fine-grained features) with compelling visual evidence (Figure 1)
Practical utility: training-free, prior-free framework applicable to black-box models accessible only via APIs, without requiring model fine-tuning
Thorough empirical analysis including ablation studies, convergence analysis, and performance on both transductive and inductive settings
Good presentation quality with clear figures and readable exposition; algorithm convergence within 10 iterations demonstrates practical efficiency
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core components (optimal transport, GMM clustering, ensemble learning) are standard techniques; the contribution amounts to combining them with squared Frobenius products, which feels incremental

Insufficient theoretical justification: why does squaring the Frobenius product yield better adaptive weighting? The explanation in Appendix 6.2 is informal; no principled justification for this specific formulation choice

Overstated novelty claims: claiming to be 'the first work to systematically investigate complementary strengths' is misleading when the work essentially applies standard ensemble methods to existing model outputs

Questionable necessity of joint optimization: ablation shows coupling T and Θ provides only modest improvements (0.3-0.8%, Fig. 4), suggesting decoupled learning may be sufficient and the added complexity unjustified
GMM assumptions lack justification: using Gaussian mixtures with diagonal covariances is a strong assumption applied without rigorous justification to arbitrary high-dimensional visual features

Experimental rigor issues: no statistical significance testing, no error bars or confidence intervals, all results appear single-run; missing simple baselines (weighted averaging of probability matrices)

Fairness of comparisons: different model combinations across datasets make attribution difficult; SOTA often uses domain-specific models (GeoRSCLIP, CONCH) while baselines use vanilla models, conflating method contribution with model selection
'Prior-free' claim needs qualification: model selection itself is a prior; fixed entropy weight ε=0.01 is not validated; equal weight initialization and GMM components=K are design choices
Limited failure analysis: no investigation of when/why method works; missing analysis of correlated models, equally-good models, or worst-case scenarios

Generalization concerns: all experiments use specific models (CLIP variants, DINOv2/v3); unclear if method transfers to other foundation models or domains; domain-specific model choices appear cherry-picked
Computational costs under-analyzed: SOTA is slower than ADAP baseline (0.95s vs 0.26s) and uses more memory (1435 vs 1089 MiB), limiting practical appeal despite claimed efficiency
Missing hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: entropy weight ε, temperature τ, number of iterations not studied; hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clear articulation of complementary weaknesses in VLMs (over-reliance on textual priors) and VFMs (lack semantic alignment), effectively demonstrated in Figure 1

Comprehensive experimental validation: 26 datasets across three distinct domains (natural images, medical pathology, remote sensing) with both transductive and inductive settings; strong empirical improvements (+3.3% natural, +6.5% remote sensing, +7.9% medical over prior SOTA)
Practical and training-free approach: No fine-tuning required, works with black-box models via API, converges rapidly (~5 iterations), competitive computational efficiency
Elegant self-adaptive mechanism: Principled derivation showing how squared Frobenius inner product naturally induces adaptive weighting via MM algorithm, eliminating manual weight tuning
Thorough ablation studies: Systematic analysis of VFM importance, self-adaptive mechanism, and joint learning components (Figure 4) demonstrating contribution of each part
Competitive performance in inductive setting: Shows comparable or superior results vs. test-time adaptation methods (Table 4), improving practical applicability
Clear methodology and reproducibility: Detailed optimization procedure, implementation details provided, convergence analysis included
weaknesses: Moderate novelty: Optimal transport for ensembling and GMM fitting are established techniques; main contribution is their specific combination via squared inner product, which feels somewhat incremental

Self-adaptive mechanism provides only modest isolated gains: Figure 4 and Table 5 show improvements of 0.2-1.4% when comparing adaptive vs. non-adaptive weighting, raising questions about complexity-benefit tradeoff

Experimental confounding: Most comparisons mix different model combinations (SOTA uses CLIP+DINOv2/v3, baselines use single models), conflating gains from the integration method with gains from simply adding stronger models like DINOv3; fair ablation would compare single-model versions

Limited mechanistic understanding: Insufficient explanation of why adding semantic-agnostic VFM features helps VLMs; the coupling mechanism (Eq. 8) is interesting but underexplored; no analysis of model diversity or correlation effects
Transductive setting dominance: Most impressive results require access to test data at inference time, limiting practical applicability; inductive results (Table 4) are competitive but less dramatic

Unvalidated GMM assumptions: Assumes features fit K Gaussian mixtures (one per class); no analysis of when this fails (multi-modal classes, imbalance), or covariance estimation stability with limited samples

Missing simple baselines: No comparison with average/voting of model predictions or fixed-weight ensembles learned on small validation sets; unclear how much improvement comes from optimal transport vs. simple adaptive weighting
Hyperparameter choices unexplored: Temperature τ=0.01 and entropy ϵ=0.01 fixed without justification or sensitivity analysis; unclear if these are optimal
No statistical testing: Lacks error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; some experimental results [8,60] from prior work rather than re-implemented consistently
Insufficient failure case analysis: No discussion of dataset characteristics where SOTA underperforms; Figure 2 radar charts lack quantitative variance analysis across datasets
